# toml++ 3.4.0

The private parser header is the upstream [3.4.0 single-header release](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marzer/tomlplusplus/v3.4.0/toml.hpp), commit `30172438cee64926dc41fdd9c11fb3ba5b2ba9de`. Its unmodified SHA-256 is `6b5172ad4dd6519aec67b919181fa7a38a2234131e5b2afa232dfe444819783e`; the patched header SHA-256 is `291ae61255e4dd66472d0f4cb45da61eef3ead3e2e26fc2db130550109a7c7bd`. MIT license: [notice](../../docs/licenses/tomlplusplus.txt).

The local patch uses fallible empty initialization for parser buffers and array storage, copies string keys instead of invoking MSVC Debug noexcept string moves, and removes `noexcept` from array/table default and move constructors and move assignments, from the parser result conversion, and from the throwing-mode parse-error constructors (which allocate their message). MSVC Debug STL container initialization or move can allocate iterator proxies; an allocation failure must propagate to the parser staging boundary instead of terminating. The patch also disables the optional macro-selected configuration header and makes the two header-availability probes explicit, so the native-input attestation can enumerate the entire include closure. The parser additionally admits at most 128 segments per dotted key and 1,024 key segments per document; these limits bound recursive graph destruction and report capacity rather than invalid TOML. A malformed table header is rejected before the upstream key assertion (toml-test `invalid/key/single-open-bracket.toml`). Three literal operator declarations use the non-deprecated C++ spelling to avoid MSVC C5311. No other grammar or data model logic is changed. A focused x64 Debug injected-allocation probe covered representative valid, invalid, duplicate and nested inputs; all native profiles and the integrated allocation sweep remain required before qualification.
